title: FTC-reported Walmart wire-transfer checks move a fraud remedy into dispatch while cashing remains unverified
source_unit: FTC Walmart wire-transfer fraud-remedy announcement, case page, and timeline record
geography: United States consumers affected by fraud-induced Walmart wire transfers

denominator.unit: affected consumers reported as receiving checks

remedy_stage.value: checks being sent to affected consumers

cashing_window.unit: days to cash the reported checks

delivery_and_cashing.unit: missing individual mailing, delivery, cashing, returned-check, reissue, and receipt outcomes

observations.method: Bounded extraction from the official FTC announcement and its linked case/timeline materials, with the project event ledger retained as the reproduction layer. Aggregate dispatch, recipient count, and cashing window are not converted into a receipt or recovery rate.
observations.uncertainty: The public announcement does not disclose individual check amounts, original transfer losses, delivery failures, returned checks, cashing, or household recovery. The 65,022 figure is an aggregate program count, not a retained person-level denominator.
observations.subgroup: Consumers affected by fraud connected to Walmart wire-transfer services; the public record does not expose demographic, financial, disability, language, or access subgroups.
observations.counterinterpretation: Sending checks creates a formal remedy route while leaving delivery, cashing, amount adequacy, and residual-loss risk unresolved for individual recipients.

related_sources.claim: The FTC case page provides the enforcement and settlement context for the wire-transfer remedy.
The FTC timeline records the October 15, 2026 payment-dispatch event.
The FTC reports more than $9.8 million in checks to 65,022 consumers and a 90-day cashing instruction.

boundary: This record follows a named consumer-redress route from alleged wire-transfer control failures to reported check dispatch. It does not establish individual delivery, cashing, adequacy, original-loss recovery, fraud recurrence, trust, switching, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact official-page-derived event ledger retained at analysis/projects/us-customer-automation-recourse/data/ftc-walmart-wire-transfer-refund-dispatch-event-ledger-v1.json; direct page access was rate-limited during canonical promotion.
